newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates gain amid bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates gain amid bargain hunting.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates surged on Tuesday as international prices rose and spinners chased quality stocks, fearing a shortfall, dealers said.

"Most spinners believe that quality cotton will not be available after December 15," dealer Nasim Usman said, but added: "I think the rates have already peaked and may remain steady to weak in the coming sessions."
He said rising international prices had halted imports for the moment and encouraged ginners to push up local prices.
In the kerb market NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,350 rupees ($58.42) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
